title: Texas Police Officer Dragged as Suspect Tries to Steal his Patrol Car
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Seagoville, Texas — On July 27, 2025, just after 7 p.m., Seagoville Police Officers spotted 36-year-old Brandon Roy Boothe driving a stolen Chevrolet pickup truck. After leading police on a chase, at one point driving the wrong way on Interstate 20, Boothe crashed into another vehicle and took off on foot. When a pursuing officer attempted to subdue him with a Taser, Boothe doubled back, jumped into a marked Seagoville police SUV, and engaged in a struggle with the officer, later identified as Sgt. Ethan Sinclair. During the altercation, Boothe shifted the vehicle into gear, crashing it into the stolen truck and reversing with Sinclair partially outside, dragging the officer across the pavement.

The struggle for control of the patrol vehicle lasted over two minutes before a second officer arrived and deployed a Taser, bringing Boothe into custody. Two handguns and ammunition were later discovered inside the stolen pickup. Sgt. Sinclair sustained facial and leg injuries but was treated on scene and is expected to recover. Boothe, described by police as a known member of the white supremacist gang Peckerwood, was on parole and had a warrant for a violation issued by the Texas Department of Corrections. With a criminal record spanning nearly two decades and more than 20 prior arrests, Boothe now faces several new felony charges, including robbery, aggravated assault on a public servant, and unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon.
